$meta.purpose: Term list that constrains BOTH the curated translation of the worksheet's core text and the runtime translation of team-entered answers, so the same concept is never rendered two different ways in the same session.
$meta.status: SEED — every entry needs confirmation by an Indonesian-speaking Bible-translation practitioner before the Bali workshop. Entries flagged needsReview are the ones held with least confidence; the unflagged ones are established Indonesian biblical or literary vocabulary.
$meta.selection: Terms were chosen by frequency in the actual worksheet rather than from a generic list. The highest-leverage entries are genre (124 occurrences), Required (28), passage (26), Common (25), and feature/features (32) — the Required/Common distinction alone carries the app's core marking system.
$meta.counts: Run `npm run i18n:report -- id` for live term and review counts; a hard-coded number here would drift.

notes: Tokens in braces are substituted by the app at render time. They must appear in the translation exactly as written, including the braces, or the user reads a sentence with a hole in it.
Where Indonesian has no settled equivalent for a technical term, keep the English and gloss it once in parentheses on first use rather than coining a new word.
Match the plain-language register of the English: these prompts are read aloud to community members, not to academics.

terms.note: Indonesian borrows 'genre' in literary and translation contexts; 'jenis' is too general and would read as 'type of thing'.
Established Indonesian Bible-study term for a delimited portion of Scripture. Use 'bagian' only where the English clearly means a general part rather than a Scripture portion.
The app's marking for a feature a genre must have to be recognised as that genre. Keep capitalised as a label; it is a category name, not a description.
The app's marking for a feature often present but not necessary. 'Lazim' (customary) carries 'usually there' better than 'umum' (general), which readers hear as 'ordinary'.
'Ciri' (distinguishing trait) is the right word for a genre's characteristics. Avoid 'fitur', which is software vocabulary.
How alive and actively used a genre still is. 'Vitalitas' is also understood but reads clinically.
For a rhythmic recited or intoned form. 'Nyanyian ritmis' is a clearer description if 'kidung' reads too hymn-like in the local setting.
General saying. Use 'Amsal' only for the biblical book.
'Ibadah' for the corporate act; 'penyembahan' where the English stresses adoration specifically.
A line of poetry. Not 'garis', which is a drawn line.
Standard borrowed term in Indonesian biblical studies for paired poetic lines.
The occasion and manner of performing. 'Pertunjukan' implies a staged show and is wrong for a domestic or ritual setting.
Literally 'listeners', which fits oral genres better than 'penonton' (viewers).
Speaker of a language. Use 'pembicara' only for someone addressing an audience.
'Masyarakat' for the people as a society; 'komunitas' for a smaller defined group.
'Sukacita' is the register used in Indonesian Scripture; 'kegembiraan' is everyday happiness.
